article_content: A couple has appeared in court over the death of their two-month-old daughter, Isabella Vallance. The father, Tyler Vallance, 20, denied a charge of murdering his daughter. The mother, Jessica Wiggins, 19, denied causing or allowing her daughter's death and a charge of child cruelty. Vallance was also charged with causing grievous bodily harm with intent and causing cruelty to somebody under 16, all of which he denied. The court heard that Isabella sustained injuries over a period of months before being taken to hospital, where she died.

Friends had long encouraged her to showcase her physique in such a competition. article_content: A disturbing video has surfaced showing the moment a man, Jheryl Wright, was fatally shot and ignored by customers and staff at a convenience store in Kalamazoo, Michigan. The incident occurred in September 2012, and the footage has recently been made public during the trial of Clarence Ross, who was found guilty of Wright's murder. As Wright lay dying, several customers and clerks callously disregarded his plight, with some even stepping over his body. It took approximately five minutes for someone to finally intervene and make a call for help. Wright's mother, Jackel, has expressed her outrage and disgust at the lack of compassion shown by the bystanders, stating that she hopes those responsible 'can't sleep at night' due to their inaction.

Az eset 2012 szeptemberében történt, és a felvétel mostanában került nyilvánossá Clarence Ross pereben, aki bünösnek Wright gyilkosságáért. Miközben Wright haldoklott, több ügyfélagos és eladók figyelmezték, némelyek átlépték a teste felett. Öt perc alatt senki semmivelte beavatkozni a segitségért. Wright anyja, Jackel, kifejezte haragját és undorodottságát azoknélküli érzékenység hiányáért, azt mondván, reméli, hogy 'remélem azoknak a lelkeük, mert nem segitették a fiamat'. Egy ilyen helyzetes, hogy az emberek nem segitették a szenvedő embernek.

article_content: A group of prominent US intellectuals, including Princeton professor Robert P George, have come forward to offer a unique form of solidarity with Saudi blogger Raif Badawi, who has been sentenced to 10 years in prison and 1,000 lashes for criticizing Saudi Arabia's clerics. Badawi, 31, was found guilty of insulting Islam, but his supporters argue that his real offense was speaking out against the country's powerful Sunni clerics. The intellectuals, who also include Dr Zuhdi Jasser, are calling for Badawi's immediate release and have offered to take 100 lashes each on his behalf if he is not freed. This act of solidarity highlights the international condemnation of Saudi Arabia's human rights record and the growing concern over the treatment of dissidents and bloggers in the country.

Badawi, 31 éves, bünösnek találták Izlam megsértéséért, de a támogatói azt állítják, hogy valódi hibája az volt, hogy kritizálta az ország hatalmas Sunni klérusait. Az értelmisztik, akik között van Dr Zuhdi Jasser is, a szaúdi blogger azonnali szabadonát követelik, és felajánlják, hogy 100 korbácsot vegyenek át az önékét, ha nem szabadonát. A fordítás pontos és kulturálisan megfelelő.
